bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in the attributes code where uninitialized memory is freed, potentially leading to undefined behavior.
bug_description.normalized: While compiling the staged PHP script, PHP reaches the parameter attribute `<<A1(self::class, s->getAtelf::FOO)>>`. `zend_compile_attributes()` materializes a two-argument AST list for that attribute, and `zend_add_attribute()` allocates a `zend_attribute` whose flexible `argv[]` array has room for two `zval` slots but leaves them uninitialized. The compiler then stores the first argument successfully, but the second argument is a dynamic class-constant expression, so `zend_compile_const_expr_class_const()` raises the compile-time fatal "Dynamic class names are not allowed in compile-time class constant references" before `attr->argv[1]` is written. During request shutdown, the stored attribute is destroyed through `free_attribute()`, which blindly runs `zval_ptr_dtor()` for both slots because `attr->argc` is still 2. On the crashing execution, the uninitialized second slot is interpreted as a refcounted pointer and AddressSanitizer reports a wild READ in `zend_gc_delref`.

source.description: First project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled attribute arguments on the vulnerable path. For the staged parameter attribute, this statement produces a `ZEND_AST_ARG_LIST` with two children: a valid first argument (`self::class`) and the invalid dynamic class-constant second argument (`s->getAtelf::FOO`).
source.value_from: The staged `poc` PHP script contains the parameter attribute `<<A1(self::class, s->getAtelf::FOO)>>`; when `zend_compile_params()` reaches that attribute, `el->child[1]` becomes a two-child `args` list consumed by the compiler here.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `zend_gc_delref()` dereferences the bogus `zend_refcounted_h *` extracted from the uninitialized `attr->argv[1]` slot during attribute cleanup, producing the reported wild-address READ.

root_cause.description: The flexible `attr->argv[]` storage is allocated from raw `pemalloc()` memory and vulnerable code does not initialize each slot to `IS_UNDEF` before later population and cleanup. Because the attribute is inserted into the attribute hash before all arguments are compiled, any fatal error during argument compilation leaves trailing `argv[]` slots uninitialized but still subject to destruction. The fix adds a loop that applies `ZVAL_UNDEF(&attr->argv[i])` for every declared argument.

tainted_value_origin.description: The staged parameter-attribute AST carries the vulnerability-relevant attacker data: `args->children == 2`, and `args->child[1]` is the dynamic class-constant expression `s->getAtelf::FOO` that later aborts constant-expression compilation.

parser_admitted.description: The libFuzzer harness hands the exact staged PHP script buffer to the engine. Source scoring begins later inside `zend_compile_attributes()`, but this is the saved entry from the harness into project code.

coarse_trace.summary: The parameter attribute from the staged PHP script is compiled into an argument AST list with two children, and that child count is passed to attribute creation.
A `zend_attribute` with two `argv[]` slots is allocated and inserted into the op-array attribute hash without initializing those slots to `IS_UNDEF`.
The first attribute argument is stored, but the second argument is rejected as a dynamic compile-time class-constant reference before `attr->argv[1]` is written.
Request-shutdown cleanup destroys the stored attribute and iterates over both declared argument slots because `attr->argc` is still 2.
The destructor path interprets the uninitialized second slot as a refcounted pointer and crashes with the saved AddressSanitizer wild READ.

fine_trace.note: For the crashing parameter attribute, this materializes the attacker-controlled argument list from the parsed PHP AST. In the staged witness the list has two children: child 0 is the valid constant expression `self::class`, and child 1 is the invalid dynamic class-constant expression `s->getAtelf::FOO`.

fine_trace.code: zend_attribute *attr = zend_add_attribute(attributes, 0, offset, name, args ? args->children : 0);
fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled argument count is consumed here. Because `args->children == 2` for the crashing attribute, the compiler requests a new `zend_attribute` sized for exactly two `argv[]` elements.

The allocation includes raw storage for the flexible `argv[]` array. In the vulnerable version, none of those `zval` slots are initialized to `IS_UNDEF` before later use; the fix adds that missing initialization loop.
The attribute records `argc == 2`. Later cleanup uses this field as the loop bound, so both `argv[0]` and `argv[1]` will be destroyed even if one of them was never written.

The still-uninitialized attribute object is inserted into the op-array attribute hash before argument compilation finishes. If compilation aborts later, hash destruction will still reach this same `attr` object through the registered attribute destructor.

On the first loop iteration (`j == 0`), the constant expression `self::class` is accepted and a defined value is written into `attr->argv[0]`. The attribute object is now only partially initialized: slot 1 is still raw `pemalloc()` memory.

fine_trace.code: if (class_ast->kind != ZEND_AST_ZVAL) { zend_error_noreturn(E_COMPILE_ERROR, "Dynamic class names are not allowed in compile-time class constant references"); }
fine_trace.note: When the second attribute argument `s->getAtelf::FOO` is compiled, its class operand is dynamic rather than a `ZEND_AST_ZVAL`, so this compile-time fatal is raised. Control never reaches the stores in `zend_const_expr_to_zval()` for `attr->argv[1]`, leaving that second slot uninitialized.

During request shutdown after the compile error, the op-array attribute hash is destroyed. Because step 5 already inserted the attribute object, hash destruction invokes the registered attribute destructor on this stored entry; the sanitizer stack shows `zend_hash_destroy -> attr_free -> free_attribute`.

Cleanup iterates over every declared argument slot. Because step 4 set `attr->argc` to 2, the second loop iteration (`i == 1`) calls `zval_ptr_dtor(&attr->argv[1])` even though step 7 left that slot uninitialized.

On the crashing execution, the uninitialized bytes in `attr->argv[1]` make `Z_REFCOUNTED_P(zval_ptr)` evaluate true, so `Z_COUNTED_P(zval_ptr)` interprets the same garbage bytes as a `zend_refcounted *`. `ref` is therefore a bogus high-valued pointer derived directly from the uninitialized slot.

ASan crash site. `GC_DELREF(ref)` dereferences the bogus pointer from step 10 as `p`, and `zend_gc_delref()` immediately reads `p->refcount`. AddressSanitizer reports this as the saved `SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` at `Zend/zend_types.h:1148`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The saved ASan trace does not report the `pemalloc()` origin of the uninitialized `argv[]` storage, but the fix hunk and vulnerable source both place that missing initialization in `zend_add_attribute()`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `/bin/arvo run` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` in `zend_gc_delref` while processing the staged `poc` PHP script.

format.name: PHP script for php-fuzz-parser
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact PHP script in `poc`. The source-grounded trigger proven here is that its first parameter attribute is `<<A1(self::class, s->getAtelf::FOO)>>`: the attribute declares exactly two arguments, the first one (`self::class`) is accepted and written into `attr->argv[0]`, and the second one is a dynamic class-constant expression that triggers the compile-time fatal in `zend_compile_const_expr_class_const()` before `attr->argv[1]` is written. This GT is grounded only for witnesses that reproduce that same partial-initialization relation in the vulnerable source; it does not generalize to all attribute compilation failures.
